predecessors.name: Mughal Empire
predecessors.text: upper Sindh, the part of Sind north of about 26 N

ledger.x: 1701: Yar Muhammad Kalhoro is made subahdar of upper Sindh.
1736: bridging, page silent on the acquisitions.
1765: Ghulam Shah Kalhoro holds the conquered Kutch territories.
1768: the court moves from Khudabad to Hyderabad.
1770: Ghulam Shah Kalhoro returns the towns to the Rao of Cutch.
1783: the Talpurs overthrow the Kalhoras at Halani.
1783: the Kalhora dynasty ends with Abdul Nabi Kalhoro.

wars.name: Nader Shah's invasion of India
wars.outcome: "in 1739, during Nader Shah's invasion of India, Mian fled to Umerkot for shelter but was captured by the King of Iran" (Noor Mohammad Kalhoro page); the Kalhora page says the dynasty "succumbed to the invasion of Nader Shah" (undated).

wars.name: Durrani conquest of Sindh
wars.outcome: Ahmad Shah Durrani conquered Sind "in 1748-1750" and made it a vassal of the Durrani Empire; the page gives no tribute figure and no territorial loss.

wars.name: Kalhora attacks on Kutch
wars.outcome: Ghulam Shah Kalhoro attacked Cutch in 1763-64 (hundreds of Kutchi died in the battle near Jara) and again in 1765; Rao Godji II made a truce after losing several territories, and Busta Bandar, Lakhpat and others were returned after the 1770 marriage.

wars.name: Battle of Halani
wars.outcome: The Talpur mirs under Mir Fateh Ali Khan overthrew the Kalhoras and founded the Talpur dynasty.

certainty.note: Subah and tribal districts; the pages give no boundaries.
